title: Finite-stage killing of a class
statement:
Let $(T,T_0)$ be an affine henselian pair, let $F$ be torsion, and let $c\in
H^q(T_0,F|_{T_0})$ with $q>0$. Suppose $c$ vanishes after pullback to an
integral strictly local cover that is the inverse limit of finite, finitely
presented covers $T_\lambda\to T$. Then $c$ already vanishes after pullback to
one $T_{\lambda_0}$.

proof.text: Obtain the full cohomology colimit cocone, its stage and limit isomorphisms, and compatible restriction maps r_j from exists_cofiltered_etale_cohomology_cocone.

The vanishing hypothesis and injectivity of the limit comparison imply B_j₀(r_j₀(x))=B_j₀(0). Forgetting abelian groups preserves the small filtered colimit. Mathlib IsColimit.eq_iff′ therefore gives an arrow j₀→j in J opposite along which r_j₀(x) becomes zero. Compatibility of r gives r_j(x)=0; applying the stage isomorphism e_j proves π_j^*(x)=0.

proof_origin.place: 09YQ followed by Mathlib CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.eq_iff′; M2 stage-3 Lean proof

blueprint_sketch.statement:
In an affine henselian pair, if a positive-degree class $c$ dies on an
integral strictly-local cover $T_\infty\to T_0$ represented by a filtered
system $\{T_\lambda\}$ of finite finitely presented covers, then there exists
$\lambda_0$ such that the pullback of $c$ to $H^q(T_{\lambda_0},F|)$ is zero.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Represent the chosen cochain and its null-homotopy on the limit by finitely
many sections. Each section and each equality occurs at some index because
the system is filtered and the etale site is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Choose one index dominating those finitely many indices. The descended
cochain and the descended null-homotopy satisfy the coboundary equation at a
further finite index; replacing by that index gives $\lambda_0$. This exposes the indexing and
vanishing witness requested by Tag `09ZD`.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $(D_j)_{j\in J}$ a cofiltered system of quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes over $S$ with structure maps $\pi_j:D_j\to S$ and
affine transition morphisms, and let $X=\varprojlim_jD_j$ with projections
$p_j:X\to D_j$. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $S_{\Et}$ and
$c\in H^q(S,G)$. If the pullback of $c$ along $\pi_{j_0}\circ p_{j_0}:X\to S$
vanishes for some $j_0$, then there is $j$ such that already the pullback of
$c$ to $D_j$ vanishes.

(In the application, $(T,T_0)$ is an affine henselian pair, the $D_j$ are the
closed fibres of a system of finite, finitely presented covers $T_\lambda\to T$
whose limit is an integral strictly local cover, and $c$ is a class on $T_0$.)

proof.text:
By the continuity of etale cohomology along cofiltered limits of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps
[lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity], the pullback maps induce an
isomorphism

$$
 \varinjlim_jH^q(D_j,\pi_j^{-1}G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,G|_X).
$$

The element of the colimit represented by $\pi_{j_0}^*c$ maps to the pullback
of $c$ to $X$, which is zero; hence it is zero in the filtered colimit, so
there is $j\to j_0$ with $\pi_j^*c=0$ (the pullbacks of $c$ along the
$\pi_j$ are compatible with the transition maps).
